name: Seismic Sense

abilities.text: Look at the top X cards of your library, where X is the number of lands you control. You may reveal a creature or land card from among them and put it into your hand. Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order.

notes: X is the count expression lands-you-control. optional is the 'You may' (none need be taken), filter the creature-or-land restriction, and rest/order the random bottom. 'reveal' was DROPPED after a judge verdict: game.ts:1090 reveals the WHOLE looked-at set publicly before any choice, so dig {reveal: true} broadcasts the top X of the library instead of the at most one card this card reveals. Under-revealing the single taken card is the smaller deviation than leaking X cards of hidden information (CR 701.16a).

issues: You may reveal a creature or land card from among them and put it into your hand. — expected At most one card — the one taken — becomes public; the rest stay hidden. — scripted dig without `reveal`, so nothing is formally revealed. Deliberate and correct-by-comparison: game.ts:1134 applies reveal to the WHOLE looked-at set before any choice, which would leak X cards. In practice the deviation is near-zero because game.ts:1159 already emits {type:'library', action:'dig', found: taken names} publicly, so the taken card's identity is disclosed anyway; only knowledge.knownInHand tracking is missed. — CR CR 701.16a

Look at the top X cards of your library, where X is the number of lands you control. — expected X counted on resolution from lands you control. — scripted look {count:'lands-you-control'}, evaluated by amt() at resolution. Correct. — CR CR 608.2h

You may … Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order. — expected Taking is optional; the remainder goes to the bottom in random order. — scripted take:1 with optional:true (game.ts:1141 passes exact:!e.optional, so zero is allowed), filter {types:['Creature','Land']} gating what may be taken, rest:'bottom', order:'random' (rng.shuffle). Correct. The 0.59 render score is a renderer that prints neither the 'may' nor the random order, not a script gap.

You may reveal a creature or land card from among them and put it into your hand. — expected Exactly one card - the one taken - is revealed; the rest of the looked-at cards stay hidden, and taking nothing is allowed. — scripted dig with take:1, optional:true, filter {types:['Creature','Land']}. game.ts:1137-1141 applies the filter only to the take pool and passes exact:false when optional, so 'you may' and the creature-or-land restriction are exact. `reveal` is deliberately dropped: game.ts:1135 would reveal the WHOLE looked-at set publicly. The taken card is therefore never revealed - a deliberate under-reveal, strictly smaller than the alternative over-reveal, and the only remaining deviation on this card. — CR CR 701.16a / 701.15a

Look at the top X cards of your library, where X is the number of lands you control. — expected X counted on resolution from lands you control. — scripted look {count:'lands-you-control'} - characteristics.ts:161 counts lands on your battlefield, evaluated as the effect applies. Correct. — CR CR 608.2h

Put the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order. — expected Every card not taken goes to the bottom, order randomised, no player choice. — scripted rest:'bottom', order:'random' - game.ts:1147-1153 shuffles the remainder and pushes it to the bottom with no prompt. Correct. — CR CR 701.16a
